title: GNSS
src: R.K. Bali — Air Navigation, Part III Ch 9 (key read from the printed answer grid, PDF p. 293)

qs.q: Position fixing by satellite is by means of:
o: simultaneous bearings from a number of satellites
range and bearing from each known satellite's position
simultaneous ranges from a number of satellites
the time difference between the transmission of the satellite's coded signal and the time that it is received at the aircraft
the time difference between the satellite and the aircraft GPS unit transmitting the same code point on the signal
the correction applied to the 'raw' GPS position to obtain a more precise position

qs.q: The reason that the satellites of GPS and GLONASS do not collide is:
o: the GPS orbit is at 55° to the equator while the GLONASS is at 60°
the GPS satellite orbits are 1200 km higher than the GLONASS orbits
GLONASS has only three orbital planes while GPS has six orbital planes
qs.ex: The book: GPS orbits about 1200 km above GLONASS.

o: only provide position in latitude and longitude

The US DoD degrades GPS accuracy:
o: to prevent 100% reliance on a system which may have to be interrupted for military purposes at a moment's notice

qs.q: The accuracy of range measurement of satellite to GPS receiver is:
o: seriously reduced during periods of sunspot activity
seriously eroded during periods of anomalous propagation in an inversion
derived from accurate timepieces in the satellite and the aircraft's GPS receiver

qs.q: Satellites used in GNSS, orbit the earth:
qs.ex: GPS orbital period is 11 h 58 min: about twice a day.

qs.q: Satellite geometry error is greatest when:
qs.ex: GDOP is worst when the satellites are close together (poor cuts between position lines).

qs.q: It may be claimed that GNSS has the advantage over other air navigation systems in that it:
o: is basically a military-based system made available to civil users with solar- powered satellites which have an infinite life
has no possible input by the pilot
